newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan passes law extending leases for U.S. bases.
newsitem.headline: Japan passes law extending leases for U.S. bases.

text.p: Japan's parliament on Thursday enacted a key bill to extend leases on land for U.S. military bases on the island of Okinawa, enabling the central government to override local landowners' opposition to the contracts.

The approval by a majority in the Upper House, which follows a similar vote in the Lower House last Friday, allows Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto to ignore a May 14 deadline on the expiry of leases on private land for U.S. bases.

The law gives Tokyo a temporary extension of the leases after the current contracts expire. It will allow the government to avoid illegally occupying the plots of land owned by 3,000 anti-base activists on Okinawa, where 75 percent of U.S. installations in Japan are located.
Passage of the law clears a key political hurdle for Hashimoto, who on April 25 will hold a summit in Washington with U.S. President Bill Clinton. Security issues will be a key item on the agenda.
The dispute over the U.S. bases on Okinawa flared up in September 1995 following the rape of an Okinawan schoolgirl by three U.S. servicemen.
Okinawa is home to about half of 40,000 U.S. military personnel in Japan and hosts the large Kadena U.S. Air Force base as well as the only U.S. Marine Corps unit stationed outside the United States.
